title: ADA Tells Dentists to Question MetLife Payment Offsets After Continued Reports
html:
The American Dental Association is advising dentists who receive a recoupment request, payment offset, or overpayment recovery notice from MetLife to ask the insurer for a detailed explanation of why the recovery was generated, ADA News reported Nov. 16.

The advice follows continued reports that MetLife has been reducing, or offsetting, payments owed to ADA member dentists to recoup overpayments it allegedly made to other, unaffiliated dentists. MetLife had said in 2025 that it would modify aspects of its overpayment recovery practices after the ADA raised concerns.

Last year’s recoupments occurred when dentists separately provided care to the same patient or to different family members covered under the same dental benefit policy. At the time, MetLife told the ADA in an email that it would change its policy to offset claim overpayments only from the provider it had overpaid. It said it expected the systems changes to be complete by the end of 2025.

Dentists then sent the ADA more reports that their payments had been reduced to recover overpayments involving other offices. On Oct. 19, the ADA contacted MetLife to ask whether the policy changes had been fully implemented. MetLife responded that its current policy is not to recover an overpayment made to one provider by offsetting payments owed to an unrelated provider. It characterized the examples the ADA provided as isolated processing errors that were later corrected and said they do not reflect a policy shift.

The ADA recommends that dentists ask MetLife for the reason for the alleged overpayment, the name of the provider associated with it, the recovery methodology used, and information about any related claim adjustments. Some recovery efforts may involve 6 Degrees Health, and dentists can seek information from that company as well. The ADA is asking members to report their experiences to dentalbenefits@ada.org.

Bertram Hughes, chair of the ADA Council on Dental Benefit Programs, said the association is monitoring member reports to determine whether they align with the policy MetLife described. He said the ADA will continue to advocate for transparent and fair overpayment recovery practices and will assess whether additional action is warranted.

Sources:
ADA News, “ADA responds to continued reports of MetLife offsetting payments owed to dentists,” Nov. 16, 2026: adanews.ada.org/2026/november/metlife-offsetting-payments
